items.title: Love for pumpkin spice
items.text: The average pumpkin spice blend has cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, cloves, and allspice, and for many consumers, it gives the warm, fuzzy feelings. For centuries, people have associated the pumpkin spice flavor with fall. Early American settlers used the same ingredients to preserve the fall harvests of meat, fruit, and vegetables. In 1976, Amelia Simmons wrote a recipe for the flavor in the first American cookbook. In 1934, McCormick made the flavor official with the name pumpkin pie spice. The company gave an easy method to get all the spices needed for pumpkin pie in one shake. In the early 1990s, Starbucks capitalized on the flavor, and the company added the pumpkin spice latte to its repertoire of seasonal drinks. Since then, Starbucks has sold more than 420 million cups in the US alone. People love pumpkin spice as its smell evokes memories. Some experts say the words pumpkin spice can spark cozy fall feelings which people crave at the end of a hot summer. Difficult words: blend (a mixture of different substances), capitalize on (to make profit from something), repertoire (all the items on stock). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

items.title: Love for pumpkin spice
items.text: Many people love pumpkin spice because it gives them warm cozy feelings. They love to drink to welcome the fall when the hot summer ends. Pumpkin spice has many spices, including cinnamon, nutmeg, and ginger, and its smell is very popular. In the 1990s, Starbucks created with the first pumpkin spice latte, and millions of people loved it. Since that time, Starbucks sold more than 420 million cups of pumpkin spice latte in the US, and the company offers it to customers in the fall and winter. The history of pumpkin spice is much older than the 1990s. Hundreds of years ago, American settlers used the same spices to preserve meat, fruit, and vegetables for the winter months. In 1976, author Amelia Simmons wrote a pumpkin spice recipe which she put in the first American cookbook. Difficult words: cozy (something that makes you feel warm and relaxed), settler (a person who moves to survive and live in a new country or area), preserve (to keep food fresh). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Love for pumpkin spice
items.text: People love pumpkin spice. The spice is a mixture of several spices. For example, they are cinnamon, nutmeg , or ginger. It smells very good. It brings happy feelings. No pumpkin is in the mixture. Some people think that Starbucks makes pumpkin spice. The recipe is much older. American settlers use the spices to keep food fresh during the winter. The foods are meat, fruit, and vegetables. In 1976, Amelia Simmons writes a pumpkin spice recipe. She puts pumpkin spice in the first American cookbook. In the 1990s, Starbucks creates the pumpkin spice latte. Many people love it. The drink helps them welcome the fall after a hot summer. Difficult words: mixture (several things put together), nutmeg (a hard seed of a tropical tree), settler (a person who lives in a new country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: 5 Canadian Universities for Indian Students Who Prefer a Smaller City
items.text: Image Source: Magnific A student moving from India to a smaller Canadian city may look forward to finding a few favourite places around campus. As the city will be home during term, a campus tour can help them picture where they would spend their time between classes. They can look for nearby outdoor space or ask about a college community and regular activities they could join. 1. Queen’s University At Queen’s University in Kingston, Campus Life provides information on student clubs, intramurals, recreational activities and volunteering in the city. Students can find activities on campus and ways to meet local people beyond it. The university has broad undergraduate and graduate choices. Applicants still need to choose the level and degree they want and meet its admission requirements. Queen’s offers incoming international first-year undergraduates early move-in access and dedicated academic and career advising. A recurring activity can give students somewhere to return after orientation. Student Academic Success Services provides writing and learning-strategy support. Students can discuss unfamiliar academic expectations there as assignments begin to require more independent work. Students considering residence should check the conditions in their offer. Residence has Living Learning Communities and interest-based options, but a bed-space commitment does not promise a particular room or building. Those conditions belong alongside the decision to study in Kingston. 2. The University of Guelph The campus is in Guelph in southwestern Ontario, with organized activities and nearby outdoor space students can use during the week. The Arboretum connects to campus through trails and forest. Outdoor space is another part of the setting to consider alongside the city’s size. At the University of Guelph , GryphLife brings together clubs, events, workshops and co-curricular opportunities. Student Volunteer Connections helps students find community volunteering that suits their interests and availability. A regular activity offers contact with people beyond orientation. International applicants from India can contact an in-country representative with admissions questions. Global Pre-Arrival Support advisors help new students with registration, housing and arrival matters. GO Transit serves the campus and provides a connection with the Toronto region. items.title: France blames Iran for cyberattack on freezers
items.text: The French government has blamed Iran for a cyberattack on supermarket freezers and refrigerators across France. The attacks happened last month. They hit around 700 supermarkets and shops. Hackers took control of the cooling systems in the fridges and freezers. Temperatures increased to more than 50 degrees Celsius. Thousands of tons of frozen food melted. Stores had to throw the food away because it was no longer safe to eat. The French Foreign Minister said the attack was on a level never seen before. France believes an Iranian cyber unit carried out the attack. Iran has strongly denied it was involved in the attacks and blamed the French government for them. Security experts have warned that cyberattacks could be more dangerous in the future. Similar attacks have already affected other European countries. A French blood bank has also been hit. Fortunately, workers stopped the blood products from being damaged. Cybersecurity expert Gerome Billois stated: "At the moment, they are attacking easy equipment, but we should be prepared to see attacks on other systems like water or electricity." Weak computer security can let hackers attack places and services, such as hospitals, airports, public transport and banks. This can put people's lives in danger. items.title: Chef fired for refusing to put pineapple on pizza
items.text: An Italian chef in Brisbane, Australia, has been fired for refusing to put pineapple on pizzas, among other reasons. He went to the Fair Work Commission to fight his dismissal, but failed to get his job back. The chef stated that topping pizzas with the tropical fruit was an "insult to his culture". He claimed he was sacked from a restaurant in May after repeatedly refusing his boss's instructions to make pineapple and ham pizzas for diners. His employer contended that the refusal was one of several workplace issues. The commission rejected the chef's application because it was submitted after the deadline. The chef has since found a job at another Italian restaurant. The question of whether pineapple belongs on pizza is a controversial one. It continues to divide public opinion. Pizza purists are aghast at the idea, but it is an established menu staple in many countries. The Hawaiian pizza was reportedly invented in Canada in 1962 after a chef used ham and pineapple as toppings. The restaurant owner expressed his opinion on it. He admitted that while the pizza was not his "absolute favourite," he would not "turn his nose up at it". Many restaurateurs insist that customers should be free to enjoy whatever ingredients and toppings they choose. Although the Hawaiian pizza is popular internationally, many Italians regard it as "culinary heresy". Buy my 1,000 Ideas and Activities for Language Teachers eBook. items.title: Man completes 28-year walk around the world
items.text: A British man has completed an amazing 28-year walk around the world. Former soldier Karl Bushby, 57, arrived home in the city of Hull in England on Monday. He started his adventure in November 1998 in Chile, South America. His plan was to walk all the way home without using cars, boats, buses, trains, or airplanes. During his journey, he travelled about 58,000 kilometres through 29 countries. He crossed frozen seas, deserts, mountains, and jungles. He also faced many dangers. These included encountering polar bears and kidnappers, and spending time in a Russian prison. His journey was expected to take 12 years. However, problems with money, visas, and borders made his trip a lot longer. Thousands of people welcomed Mr Bushby home. He was very happy to finally finish his journey. His mother was waiting outside his childhood home to greet him. Bushby joked: "Sorry to keep you waiting." He also told the cheering crowd that many people around the world had helped him get home. He said he could not have done it alone. Britain's Prime Minister congratulated him on his achievement. He praised Bushby's determination and belief in himself. Bushby told the Guardian newspaper that he wasn't so interested in walking. He said: "It's boring as hell." That didn't stop him walking across four continents. items.title: Study finds majority of pilots nod off mid-flight
items.text: A new report has raised serious concerns about pilot fatigue. The European Cockpit Association (ECA) conducted a survey of nearly 7,200 pilots across 32 countries. It discovered that exhaustion in the cockpit is a widespread and underreported problem. More than three-quarters of respondents said they had briefly dozed off while operating an aircraft in the month before the survey. Almost a quarter of them admitted they continued flying even when they were too tired. Furthermore, half said they had operated a flight when they should have declared themselves unfit for duty. Tiredness can result from long working hours, insufficient rest, and unpredictable schedules. The pilots were very frank in their answers to the survey questions. Many said they were reluctant to report fatigue because they feared punishment or other negative reactions from their bosses. Captain Coen George, a director of the ECA, warned: "When pilots fear career consequences, fatigue goes unreported and the risk returns to the cockpit." Aviation safety experts say exhaustion can impair judgement, slow reaction times and prevent pilots from responding effectively to unexpected in-flight situations. The experts urged airlines to foster a culture in which pilots can report tiredness without fear of repercussions. Carriers should ensure that passenger safety is their top priority. items.title: Sharks in an aquarium
items.text: Visitors at a South Korean aquarium watched in amazement at a shark swimming in a tank with another shark’s tail hanging out of its mouth. While sharks do not tend to eat others of the same species when they are in captivity and they have regular feeds, experts at the aquarium said that sharks have their own territory, and when they occasionally bump against each other, they bite out of astonishment . The smaller shark which fell prey to its bigger counterpart was a banded hound shark. The bigger beast was a sand tiger shark. Difficult words: tend (to do something regularly), species (a kind of animal), astonishment (great surprise), counterpart (a similar animal). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

items.title: Sharks in an aquarium
items.text: At a South Korean aquarium, a shark swam into an even bigger shark, and the bigger shark ate it! For some time, the big shark swam around, and the tail of its prey hung out of its mouth. The visitors of the aquarium looked on in amazement . Sharks do not usually eat each other in captivity , but they have to have their own territory. Difficult words: prey (an animal another animal eats), amazement (surprise, shock), captivity (not free). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Sharks in an aquarium
items.text: This news is from an aquarium . The aquarium is in South Korea. There are sharks in the aquarium. A big shark attacks a smaller shark. The big shark eats the small shark. The small shark hangs out of the big shark’s mouth. Visitors see this. They are shocked. This is rare . Usually, sharks do not eat other sharks. However, sharks can be territorial . Difficult words: aquarium (a place where you can see fish), rare (special, it does not happen often), territorial (when an animal or a person has an area which is his or her area; the animal or person protects the area). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Russell Brand goes to prison
items.text: Following the high-profile conviction of British comedian and actor Russell Brand for rape and sexual assault, UK police chiefs expect more victims to step forward. London’s Metropolitan Police Commissioner stated that successful court verdicts often give additional survivors the confidence to report past abuse, knowing they will be believed. Brand, who previously starred in Hollywood films and was once married to pop singer Katy Perry, faces a lengthy prison sentence after a London court found him guilty of raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others. He also faces ongoing investigations regarding additional allegations , including one involving a 16-year-old girl at the time of the incident. British Prime Minister praised the victims for their courage in bringing the horrific crimes to light. As one of Britain’s most prominent public figures convicted of sex offenses in recent years, Brand remains in custody and is awaiting his formal sentencing hearing. Difficult words: conviction (a formal declaration by a court of law that someone is guilty of a criminal offense), allegation (a claim that someone has done something illegal or wrong, typically one made without immediate proof), courage (the ability to do something frightening or difficult without showing fear). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

items.title: Russell Brand goes to prison
items.text: British comedian Russell Brand was found guilty of rape and sexual attack in a London court. Following the verdict, police leaders say they expect more victims to come forward with new claims. One of them explained that seeing a famous person held responsible gives other victims confidence to speak up. Brand, a former Hollywood actor once married to singer Katy Perry, now faces a long time in prison. British Prime Minister thanked the brave women who spoke out about his terrible crimes. Police are already looking into other complaints against Brand, including one from a girl who was 16 years old at the time. The 51-year-old former star will go to court for his formal sentencing . Difficult words: rape (the crime of forcing another person to have sex without their consent), victim (a person harmed, injured, or killed as a result of a crime, accident, or other event), sentencing (the official proceeding where a judge gives a verdict). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: Russell Brand goes to prison
items.text: A London court says that famous British actor Russell Brand is guilty of big crimes. He hurts four women and must now go to prison for a long time. Police say that more women will likely come and tell their stories now. The police say that it is good that women can speak. People will believe them now. The British prime minister thanks the women who tell the truth about Brand’s bad actions. Police are still looking into other stories about him. Brand will find out his time in prison soon. Difficult words: guilty (when someone is responsible for something bad they do), likely (when something may happen or be true), prime minister (the leader of a government). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

items.title: World-famous London shopping street pedestrianized
items.text: One of London's most famous shopping streets has been pedestrianized. This means no cars, buses, trucks, or motorbikes can enter it. The street is called Oxford Street. It is well known all over the world. It used to be full of traffic. The Mayor of London, Sir Sadiq Khan, decided to make it pedestrian-only. Around one kilometre of the street is off limits to vehicles. However, delivery trucks can use the area between midnight and 7 am. Mayor Khan hopes the pedestrianization will bring more shoppers back to the area. He called it a very important event for London. Mr Khan also plans to plant more trees along the street, create public squares, and add more seats and tables. There have been mixed reactions to the pedestrianization of Oxford Street. Many people support the plan. They are happy that the area will be less polluted. Khan said a traffic-free Oxford Street would "unlock the full potential" of an important area of London and help make a better, greener, and richer London. Around half a million people visit the street every day. However, many Londoners are unhappy that the street has been closed to traffic. Local official Tim Barnes said: "Traffic will be pushed to the small streets nearby causing economic and environmental harm." The Spectator magazine warned that life for car drivers would be harder. items.title: Fake bomb warnings
items.text: A wave of anonymous bomb threats continued to disrupt European aviation on Friday, following at least 25 reported scares across the continent the previous day. Control towers placed a Ryanair flight from Rome to Lisbon under high security alert after they received a call warning of an explosive device on board. The aircraft landed safely in Portugal, where security forces immediately launched thorough inspections. Simultaneously , French authorities confirmed four additional bomb alerts involving planes flying over their airspace, all of which landed safely for emergency checks. Elsewhere, a Wizz Air flight from Prague to Rome was diverted to Venice because of a similar security threat. European law enforcement agencies and judicial police have opened extensive investigations to identify the source of these widespread disruptions. While security teams have found no explosives so far, EU officials stated it remains too early to determine if the coordinated scares are linked. Difficult words: anonymous (made or done by someone whose name is not known or made public), simultaneously (happening, existing, or done at the same time), judicial police (branch of law enforcement responsible for criminal investigations and gathering evidence for legal proceedings). You can watch the video news lower on this page.
